subject: maths
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Read and write numbers up to 9999 using place value
Know the expanded form, place value and face value of digits in four-digit numbers
Count forwards and backwards from any number
Compare two numbers by place value and arrange numbers in order
Form the greatest and smallest numbers from given digits, with and without repeats
Find rules for comparing numbers by noticing patterns
Add and subtract three-digit numbers, with and without regrouping, up to 999
Estimate a sum or difference, then check the answer
Choose the right operation for a real-life problem shown in pictures or stories
Learn multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10, and see multiplication as repeated addition
Understand division as equal sharing and equal grouping, and find it by repeated subtraction
Add and subtract small amounts of money, and make simple rate charts and bills
Work out sums and differences of two-digit numbers in their head
Recognise straight and curved lines in 2D shapes
Make 2D shapes by paper folding, cutting on a dot grid, and drawing straight lines
Describe 2D shapes by counting their sides, corners and diagonals
Fill a region with one shape so there are no gaps or overlaps, and tell which shapes can do this
Make shapes with tangram pieces
Read a simple map, which need not be to scale, and draw one
Draw line pictures of 3D objects on paper
Measure length and distance in centimetres and metres with a scale or measuring tape
Understand how a metre and a centimetre are related
Estimate and check the lengths of objects nearby
Weigh objects on a simple balance using stones or other non-standard weights
Compare containers by capacity, and see that pouring does not change the amount
Find a given day and date on a calendar
Read the time to the hour on a clock or watch, and read the 12-hour and 24-hour clock
Convert between days and hours, and between hours and minutes
Collect data for a purpose and record it with tally marks
Show data as a pictograph or a bar chart
Sort and compare data
Draw conclusions from the data
Find the unit of repeat in a pattern
Extend a pattern using the unit of repeat
Create their own patterns with a unit of repeat

gaps: Teaching processes and learning resources are left out; the file lists only what a child learns.
The key concepts list multiplication tables of 7 and 9; the learning outcomes list only 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10. The file follows the outcomes.
